region: Union Springs · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Heart & Hands is the small Cayuga Lake winery of Tom and Susan Higgins. Tom grew up in the Finger Lakes, left for a career in technology, then worked in wine at Zachy’s in New York, at Château La Lagune in Bordeaux and in Finger Lakes cellars before coming home. Around 2005 he studied geological maps in search of limestone, and in 2007 the couple bought a slope a few hundred feet above the lake’s eastern shore near Union Springs. The name comes from the Irish Claddagh ring, whose hands, heart and crown stand for friendship, love and loyalty.

Petite Arvine is a rare white grape from Switzerland’s Valais, prized there for its bright acidity and a faint saline edge. The Higginses planted it, along with Aligoté, Auxerrois and Lagrein, in a 2019 expansion of their estate vineyard, which sits on Onondaga limestone and is certified under the New York Sustainable Winegrowing program. The fruit is picked by hand, basket-pressed, and fermented in small lots, some in stainless steel and some in larger neutral French oak barrels, so each block and vessel can be compared.

The winery counts 2022 among its first harvests of Petite Arvine. A warm, dry spring and a drought-like early summer gave small berries and extremely low yields, which the winery says produced deep, concentrated flavours. Its own note for this wine describes peach, lime, lychee and mango on the nose and a lively citrus-driven palate.
facts: Heart & Hands estate, planted 2019 on Onondaga limestone
